title: How the casino wins at a game that's almost 50/50
description:
A European roulette wheel has 18 red pockets, 18 black and one green zero. Bet $10 on red for 37 spins: on average you win 18 times (+$180) and lose 19 (-$190), so you're $10 down, 2.7% of everything you bet. A single number pays 35 to 1, so $1 on all 37 numbers gets $36 back: $1 lost, 2.7% again. Every bet on the table pays as if the wheel had 36 pockets; it has 37. Over a million $10 bets a night, that's about $270,000 for the house, give or take $20,000, and a losing night practically never happens.

Numbers checked in code (exact odds plus a 100,000-night simulation). Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roulette

beats.say: Roulette's nearly a coin flip, yet the house wins.
No rigged wheel. No magnets. Just one green pocket.
Bet 10 dollars on red. There are 18 red pockets, 18 black, and one green zero.
Spin 37 times. Red comes up 18. You win 180 dollars.
So you're 10 dollars down. 2.7% of everything you bet.
Fine, skip red. A single number pays 35 to 1.
Put 1 dollar on all 37 numbers. One of them wins, and you get 36 back.
Every bet on the table pays like the wheel has 36 pockets. It has 37.
You might get lucky. A million bets a night can't. The casino keeps about 270,000 dollars.
It doesn't need luck. It just needs you to keep spinning.
American wheels add a double zero. How much does the casino keep there?
